title: The stupa in the sky (Kern ch. 11)
hook: a jeweled stupa rises from the earth; an ancient Buddha inside invites the Buddha to share his seat

segments.voice: Yesterday, the preacher: anyone who carries this teaching to even one person, honored as a messenger. Your line: even one verse. Which line did you pass along? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-five.

The ground opens in the middle of the sermon. Up out of the earth, in front of the Buddha, rises a stupa, a tower built to hold the remains of a holy one, and this one is made of jewels. It doesn't stop at ground level. It climbs, and hangs there in the sky, hung with banners and bells, giving off fragrance. Then a voice comes out of it, praising the Buddha for teaching the Lotus. The whole assembly stares upward at a reliquary that speaks. Chapter eleven has begun, and it only gets stranger. Today: the stupa in the sky.
screen: `THE GROUND OPENS.` → `A JEWELED TOWER RISES.` → `A VOICE FROM INSIDE.`

segments.voice: First, the tower. A bodhisattva named Mahapratibhana asks the obvious question: what is this? The Buddha explains. Inside is the whole body of a Buddha named Prabhutaratna, Many Jewels, from a world long past, who entered final nirvana ages ago. Second, why he came. While he was still on the path, Many Jewels made a vow: wherever this sutra is taught, in any world, my stupa will rise up out of the ground to hear it, and to say, well done. So a Buddha from the far past has come as a listener, and as a witness. Third, the door. The assembly wants to see him. But the stupa won't open until the Buddha calls home every form of himself teaching across the worlds in every direction. He does. They arrive, and the worlds are made clean to hold them. Then the Buddha rises into the air and opens the stupa's door with a finger, and the text says it sounds like a great bolt sliding back on a city gate. Inside, Many Jewels sits whole, as if deep in meditation. Fourth, the seat. Many Jewels moves over and offers half of his seat. The Buddha steps in and sits down beside him. Two Buddhas, one from ages ago and one from now, side by side in a jeweled tower in the sky. Then, so the crowd below can be near them, the Buddha lifts the whole assembly up into the air to be near them. Some readers hear in the seat a picture of the teaching itself: not owned by one age, shared across them. The sutra simply shows it. One seat. Two Buddhas. Room enough.
screen: `A TOWER RISES AND SPEAKS.` · `A BUDDHA WHO CAME TO LISTEN.` · `EVERY EMANATION GATHERS FIRST.` · `HALF THE SEAT, OFFERED.` · then, large: `TWO ON ONE SEAT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: share your seat with someone. Settle where you're sitting, and feel the seat holding you up. Notice how much room you take. Now bring to mind one person you'd usually rank, above you or below you: a boss, a new hire, an older relative, a kid. In your mind, move over, and let them sit right beside you, shoulder to shoulder, nobody higher. Stay there together for a few breaths. Then let the picture go, and rest with the breath and the seat. The bell holds the time.
The stupa in the sky. A jeweled tower rises from the earth, and the Buddha of a past age inside offers the Buddha half his seat. Today's word.
screen: `THE STUPA IN THE SKY — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: two on one seat. Today, give up the better chair, or your turn, or the head of the table, and sit beside someone instead. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-five.

screen: `DAY 1165 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE DRAGON KING'S DAUGHTER (KERN CH. 11).`

howItsDone: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, the scene of Many Jewels and Shakyamuni seated together in the stupa is recited and pictured in temple art, and the two Buddhas side by side are honored together.

fork.setup: you're Many Jewels, seated in your stupa. the door opens, and the Buddha who taught the sutra stands there. what do you do?
options: stay seated and receive his bow.
move over and offer him half your seat.
step out and give him the whole seat.
fork.reveal: Many Jewels offers half his seat, and the Buddha sits down beside him: two Buddhas, past and present, side by side.

original.note: Sanskrit: a mound or tower that holds relics; here, one of jewels, rising from the earth.

trapdoor: what you thought: a stupa is a decorative tower in a temple garden.
what it means: a reliquary for a holy one's remains; here a jeweled one rises into the sky with a past Buddha inside who came to hear the sutra.
what a scholar hears: in chapter eleven the stupa's 'relic' is alive and speaking, and it shares its seat: past and present Buddhas, side by side.

notes: Chapter paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 11, not quoted (wording unverified). Check: stupa of precious substances rises and stands in the sky; voice praises Shakyamuni; Mahapratibhana asks; Prabhutaratna's vow; gathering of Shakyamuni's emanated Buddhas and purification of worlds; door opened with a finger, sound like a bolt drawn on a city gate; half-seat offered; assembly lifted into the air.
'Not owned by one age, shared across them' is attributed to 'some readers'; confirm or cut.
howItsDone: images of the two Buddhas seated side by side in temple art (e.g. in China) are well known; confirm the general phrasing.
Editor: cut the unsupported 'nobody has seen a reliquary talk before' and the invented 'craning their necks'; the lift into the air is now tied to the wish to be near the two Buddhas.
